It's the amount of land and natural resources that could be used just to keep AI growing. When we use AI, we only see the screen and the answer it gives us. We dont really see the buildings, electricity, water, and land behind it. But as AI becomes bigger, more infrastructure will be needed to support it, and that can affect the environment and the people living in those areas. For example, the Pax Silica project in New Clark City. The proposed hub covers around 4,000 acres or about 1,600 hectares and is connected to AI, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and data center infrastructure. There are already farmers and Aeta communities raising concerns because they fear losing their land, homes, and source of livelihood. Some farmers have also raised concerns about what could happen to their water supply and agricultural land.

For me, that is something people should really pay attention to. We always hear about how AI will bring jobs, investments, and new technology, but we should also ask what happens to the people and the land where these projects are built. If a technology is supposed to make the future better, then we should not ignore the people who might have to give up part of their present for it. And this is only one example. As AI companies continue building more data centers and other facilities around the world, the demand for electricity, water, and land will also increase. So the environmental problem of AI is not just about carbon emissions or electricity bills. It can reach people's homes, farms, water, and way of living. I think that is the part we should be more worried about before we keep building more and more for AI.
column11:
I think public awareness should start by making people realize how much AI has already entered our everyday lives. A lot of Filipinos are already using AI for their businesses, especially for posters, advertisements, product pictures, captions, and even songs. We also see AI being used in different trends online, and sometimes people use it just because everyone else is doing it. It has become so normal that some people dont even stop to think if they actually need AI for what they are doing.

But honestly, I dont think simply telling people to “use AI responsibly” will be enough. Many people will listen, agree for a moment, and then brush it off when they go back to their usual habits. Even if we teach them about the environmental effects, misinformation, or other problems caused by AI, some will still choose convenience because AI makes things faster and easier. For me, we also need to bring back the value of things that do not need AI at all. We should protect books, libraries, printed materials, and actual sources of information. In a way, books are our real data centers. They store knowledge without needing a server running somewhere, and they have been carrying information from one generation to another long before AI existed. We should not let our dependence on AI make us forget how valuable these things are.

We can raise awareness, but people also need to see that they have a choice. Not every poster needs to be generated by AI. Not every song needs AI. Not every trend needs AI. Sometimes we can just make things ourselves, use our own ideas, read an actual book, or learn from a real person. Responsible use of AI should not only mean knowing how to use it properly. It should also mean knowing when we simply dont need to use it.
